newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CSR sees no great building materials growth.
newsitem.headline: CSR sees no great building materials growth.

text.p: CSR Ltd Chairman Alan Coates told shareholders on Monday they should be under no illusion that the company could generate large amounts of growth in its building and construction materials division.
Coates said both were mature industries and Australia was experiencing low population growth.
"There's no way we will get extraordinary profits out of those groups," he said.
"They will improve as markets improve but they will go down as sure as night follows day when we get into another slump," he said.
Coates said CSR, a building materials, sugar and aluminium producer, would continue to close plants for some years to come in efforts to enhance the efficiency of its operations.
However, he said CSR and its two main competitors Pioneer International Ltd and Boral Ltd all faced the difficulties of intense competition and oversupply.

CSR reported a net profit of A$53.70 million for the year to March 31, 1996 for its construction materials division, down from A$62.8 million, and a net profit of A$31.20 million for its Australian building materials unit, down from A$73.4 million.
CSR shares were eight cents lower at A$5.19 at 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT) on Monday.
